documents.text:
Vicente Cárcel Orti

Vicente Cárcel Orti (born 1944) is a Spanish historian and priest who has made significant contributions to the field of Spanish history and Catholic Church studies. Early Life and Education

Vicente Cárcel Orti was born on September 25, 1944, in Valencia, Spain. He pursued his higher education at the Pontifical University of Salamanca, where he earned a degree in Ecclesiastical History. He later obtained his doctorate in History from the University of Valencia. Career

Cárcel Orti has had a distinguished career as a historian and priest. He has served as a professor of Ecclesiastical History at the Pontifical University of Salamanca and has written numerous books and articles on Spanish history, particularly on the Catholic Church's role in the country. Awards and Honors

One of the most notable honors bestowed upon Vicente Cárcel Orti is the title of "Dearest Son" (Hijo Predilecto in Spanish), a prestigious award conferred by the Autonomous Community of Valencia. This title is a mark of recognition for his outstanding contributions to the field of history and his service to the Catholic Church. According to an article published in the Spanish newspaper, Levante-EMV, on November 24, 2004, Cárcel Orti was awarded the title of "Dearest Son" by the Valencian Government in recognition of his "outstanding work in the field of history and his dedication to the Catholic Church."
